notes: The MPI4E (NEC/Sharp lists it as "MPi4e") is not a standalone box — it is a small internal "Interface Board" (55 x 40 x 4.7 mm) hosting a Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 that slides into an internal card slot on compatible NEC MultiSync ME, M, MA, and 5th-generation P-series displays, replacing the display's standard connector board. Per NEC: "internal connection for power, video, audio, data and all control interfaces" — meaning power and video/audio come from the display's internal slot (a card-edge connector), NOT from any external connector, so there is no separate power port to list. The only externally accessible connectors, visible on the card's outward-facing bracket once installed, are Ethernet + 2x USB-A ("The Ethernet and USB interfaces of the display interface board allow easy integration into a network or connection with external devices such as mouse, keyboard, and touch" per NEC) plus one additional unlabeled USB-C-shaped connector seen in official product photography that NEC's text does not document (possibly a service/OTG port). No official spec sheet/PDF with a connector table could be located — NEC's installation-guide PDF link on the product page returns 404 — so port list and grades were derived from the manufacturer's own product photos (rear-bracket shots) plus well-established Raspberry Pi CM4 platform specs (Gigabit Ethernet PHY, USB 2.0-only host ports), not from an explicit written spec. A WiFi variant exists with built-in WiFi and external antenna (antenna connector not modeled here). Confidence set to medium because the source page and photos are authoritative/official but incomplete, and grades are inferred rather than stated.

ports.name: Ethernet
ports.note: Grade inferred from the underlying Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 platform (Gigabit PHY); NEC's page only says 'Ethernet interface,' no speed stated.

ports.name: USB 1
ports.note: For mouse/keyboard/touch per NEC copy. Grade inferred from CM4 platform (USB 2.0 only); not stated by NEC.

ports.name: USB 2
ports.note: Grade inferred from CM4 platform (USB 2.0 only); not stated by NEC.

ports.name: USB-C
ports.note: Third, unlabeled connector visible on the card's rear bracket in official product photos; shape matches USB-C. Purpose (service/OTG) not documented on NEC's product page — low confidence on function, grade omitted.
